skill.name: nature-reader
skill.description: Creates full-paper Chinese-English Markdown readers from PDFs, DOI/arXiv links, publisher HTML, or pasted article text. It preserves paragraph source anchors, figure and table placement, captions, terminology notes, and draft labels.
skill.summary: Create source-grounded bilingual Markdown readers for academic papers.
skill.author: Community contribution, refactored into static/dynamic layers

No evidence found for prompt injection, shell execution, encoded payloads, or system reconnaissance.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory references load shared files outside the skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor the shared terminology ledger into the skill or replace the paths with package-local references.

content.value_statement: Full paper translation can lose figures, tables, and source context. This skill creates a grounded Markdown reader with Chinese-English blocks, source anchors, and figure placement.
actual_capabilities: Routes PDF text, scanned PDF, HTML, DOI/arXiv, and pasted text to source-specific guidance.
Produces paper.md with Original and Chinese paragraph pairs.
Builds source_map.json with page and block anchors.
Places cropped figures and tables near their first substantive mention.
Records missing, uncertain, or low-confidence content in translation_notes.md.
Supports optional reader.html output when a browser preview is requested.
limitations: Requires access to the source document or a lawfully reachable full text.
OCR quality can limit accuracy for scanned PDFs.
It is not designed for summary-only or citation-search tasks.
Browser preview output is optional and not the default artifact.

use_cases.title: Read a Research Paper
use_cases.description: Create a full bilingual Markdown reader with source anchors and figure placement.

use_cases.title: Prepare Journal Club Material
use_cases.description: Turn a paper into aligned original and Chinese sections with captions and notes.

use_cases.title: Review Translation Consistency
use_cases.description: Use the terminology ledger and source map to keep recurring technical terms consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Translate One Paper
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full Chinese-English Markdown reader for this PDF. Keep Original and Chinese blocks, source anchors, and figure captions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a readable PDF.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a DOI
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve this DOI or arXiv link, use the lawful full text if available, and build the full bilingual reader.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when only an identifier is available.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Scanned Paper
prompt_templates.prompt: This PDF is scanned. Run OCR, mark low-confidence blocks, crop figures and tables, and keep captions near related discussion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with OCR and layout uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Grounded Reader
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the full bilingual reader with terminology notes, source anchors, figure placement, and follow-up citation support. Label missing material.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a reusable reading artifact.

output_examples.input: A selectable-text PDF for a journal article.
output_examples.output: A Markdown reader with metadata, aligned Original and Chinese paragraphs, figure cards, bilingual captions, source pointers, and uncertainty notes.

output_examples.input: A DOI where only the abstract is reachable.
output_examples.output: A draft reader that separates confirmed metadata and abstract content from unretrieved body sections.

output_examples.input: A scanned conference paper with complex figures.
output_examples.output: An OCR-aware reader with low-confidence labels, cropped figure assets, captions, and page-based navigation.

best_practices: Provide the full source file or link and say whether the text is selectable.
Allow draft labels for missing, paywalled, or uncertain source content.
Review the terminology notes before reusing the translation.
anti_patterns: Ask for only a summary when you need a full translation.
Paste partial excerpts and expect complete source-grounded coverage.
Ignore low-confidence OCR notes or missing page labels.

faq.question: Can it process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses OCR guidance and marks low-confidence blocks instead of guessing.

faq.question: Does it only work for Nature papers?
faq.answer: No. It supports academic papers from PDFs, DOI/arXiv links, HTML pages, or pasted text.

faq.question: What are the main outputs?
faq.answer: The main outputs are paper.md, source_map.json, translation_notes.md, and extracted figure or table assets.

faq.question: Can it make a browser reader?
faq.answer: Yes, but reader.html is optional and only used when requested.

faq.question: How does it handle missing full text?
faq.answer: It creates a draft reader from available material and labels unretrieved sections.

faq.question: Does it answer follow-up questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It keeps source anchors so answers can point back to the original blocks.
